avoid_supplements.name: Kaolin-pectin antidiarrheals
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Reduces clindamycin absorption by binding in GI tract; may reduce antibiotic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2-3 hours; avoid concurrent use

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce CYP3A4, potentially reducing clindamycin concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Consider alternative antibiotic or monitor for reduced efficacy

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics (Saccharomyces boulardii, Lactobacillus)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Clindamycin disrupts normal flora; probiotics may help mitigate C. difficile risk during therapy
caution_supplements.action: Administer 2+ hours apart; may be beneficial adjunctive therapy

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium/calcium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Minor potential for chelation; unlikely to significantly impact clindamycin absorption
caution_supplements.action: Separate dosing by 2 hours if desired; monitor for efficacy

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals (concurrent dosing)
avoid_foods.mechanism: May delay clindamycin absorption, though oral formulation can be taken with or without food
avoid_foods.action: Take with glass of water; food is not contraindicated but may slow absorption rate

caution_foods.name: Fermented foods (yogurt, kefir, sauerkraut)
caution_foods.mechanism: Contain beneficial bacteria; disrupted by clindamycin but may help restore flora post-therapy
caution_foods.action: Continue consumption during therapy; particularly beneficial after treatment completion

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May modestly affect GI transit; clindamycin may cause diarrhea independent of diet
caution_foods.action: Maintain normal fiber intake; monitor for diarrhea severity

monitoring_notes: Monitor for Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD), the primary safety concern with clindamycin; antibiotic-induced diarrhea may be severe and warrants medical evaluation. Counsel patients to report persistent or bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, or signs of hypersensitivity.
